title: Reliability standards launch playbook
body:
Purpose
This is a practical launch playbook for a cross-functional reliability program that defines service-level objectives (SLOs), instruments the measurement pipeline, and stages a rollout across product teams. The goal is an actionable minimum-viable program (MVP) that reduces incident frequency for user-facing generation endpoints by 25% within 3 quarters, while providing a repeatable process for future services.

Audience
- SRE leads and engineers
- Product/Platform managers and owners
- Observability/Telemetry engineers
- Release and support teams

Scope (MVP)
- Define availability and latency SLOs for: hosted inference API, model warm/prefill paths, and asynchronous batch embedding jobs.
- Implement measurement for error/latency signals using existing tracing and metrics (Prometheus + Honeycomb).
- Create service-level dashboards and weekly SLO health reports.
- Run one pilot with the Search-rewrite service and one pilot with Dedicated router service.

Out of scope (MVP):
- Full organization-wide SLO rollout (phased after pilots)
- Long-term data retention or billing changes

Goals & Success Metrics
- 25% reduction in P99 latency tail for targeted routes within 9 months.
- SLO adoption in 2 pilot services and documented runbooks for on-call.
- Instrumentation coverage >= 90% for request/response paths in pilot services.
- Weekly SLO health digest automatically sent to stakeholders.

High-level timeline (quarterly milestones)
- Q1 (Weeks 0–8): Program kickoff, SLO templates, pilot selection, instrumentation spike.
- Q2 (Weeks 9–20): Implement measurement, dashboards, alert rules; run canary on Search-rewrite.
- Q3 (Weeks 21–36): Broaden coverage to Dedicated router, A/B rollout, retrospective and playbook iteration.

Milestones and owners (first 12 weeks)
- Week 0–1: Kickoff workshop (Owner: Maya Fernandez) — align stakeholders, agree pilots.
- Week 2–3: SLO template + definition guide (Owner: Arjun Mehta) — availability/latency/error budget math.
- Week 4–6: Instrumentation spike (Owner: Lina Zhang) — traces and metrics for pilot services.
- Week 6–8: Dashboards & runbooks (Owner: Oscar Rivera) — Honeycomb queries, Grafana panels, Slack alerts.
- Week 8: Pilot readiness review (Owner: Claire Nguyen) — security signoff and rollout checklist.

SLO definition patterns (recommended baseline)
- Availability SLO (control plane): % of 2xx responses for API routes over 28 days, target 99.9% for Tier-1 routes.
- Latency SLO (P95/P99): P95 < 120ms for simple route, P99 < 500ms for generation start for hosted tier. Use histogram-based buckets for stable measurement.
- Error budget policy: Cumulative error budget burn above 50% triggers an operational pause on non-essential deploys.

Instrumenting measurement pipeline
Checklist:
- Ensure each service emits request-id and trace-id (if missing: small PR to middleware).
- Expose latency histogram and status_code metric to Prometheus.
- Add sampling rules for traces so P99 traces are captured to Honeycomb/Jaeger.
- Create a derived metric for error_budget_burn in Prometheus recorded rule.
- Create Grafana dashboard panels for daily SLO attainment and 28-day rolling window.

Alerting and on-call behavior
- Alert types: (1) SLO burn urgent (>=75% of budget used in 7 days), (2) steady degradation (7-day trend), (3) instrumentation gaps (missing metric & heartbeat).
- Pager policy: SLO burn or critical degradation pages SRE primary; product owner is paged for informative context if escalation criteria met.
- Runbook snippet: immediate triage steps, relevant logs/trace links, rollback toggle path, decision tree for deployments.

Cross-functional coordination (RACI-lite)
- Define SLOs: Product (R), SRE (A), Observability (C), Platform infra (I).
- Implement instrumentation: Observability (R), SRE (C), Platform infra (C).
- Dashboards & alerts: Observability (R), SRE (A), Support (C).
- Release gating: SRE (R), Product (A), Release engineering (C).

Communication plan
- Weekly 30-minute sync (Tues 10:30am PT) for owners — cadence during pilot.
- Bi-weekly stakeholder update (email + short Confluence summary).
- Dedicated Slack channel #sre-reliability-program for async questions and rollout notes.
- Executive monthly summary for VP Eng and Head of Product.

Pilot rollout checklist (pre-canary)
- Metrics emitted for 14 days with stable tag coverage.
- Canary traffic slice defined (1–5%) and rollback plan documented.
- SLO dashboards and alerting wired to on-call.
- Load test to validate instrumentation and basic SLO assumptions.

Pilot canary execution steps
- Day 0: Enable canary slice (1% traffic) for 24 hours; compare telemetry vs baseline.
- Day 1–3: Increase to 5% if stable; monitor error budget and latency tail.
- If error budget burn >20% in 24h or P99 regression >2x, rollback and run incident review.

Training & documentation
- Short 60-minute training for product and support teams on reading SLO dashboards and responding to alerts. Owner: Claire Nguyen.
- On-call cheat sheet (one-pager) with step-by-step triage.
- Confluence page template for team SLOs with examples and definition checklist.

Dependencies & blockers
- Telemetry SDK update needed across microservices (Dependency ticket: JIRA:SRE-1289).
- Quota on tracing ingestion in Honeycomb — coordinate with Observability to increase sample budget.
- Dedicated infra for metrics retention (Platform ticket: PLATFORM-77).

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Teams perceive SLO as another compliance item -> Mitigation: emphasize product-owner benefits and tie to improved user metrics (conversion/engagement).
- Risk: Insufficient tracing coverage -> Mitigation: small middleware changes with a clear migration plan and QA steps.
- Risk: Alert fatigue -> Mitigation: conservative alert thresholds for MVP; iterate after 4 weeks.

Post-pilot evaluation (metrics to capture)
- Change in incident count attributable to target routes.
- SLO attainment percentage over 28-day windows pre/post.
- Time-to-detect and time-to-recover (MTTD/MTTR) from alerts tied to SLOs.
- Developer overhead to maintain instrumentation (measured via PR count and hours logged).

Playbook maintenance and iteration
- After pilot completion, schedule a 2-week retrospective and update templates.
- Convert successful patterns into a team onboarding kit for scaled rollout.
- Quarterly review of SLO thresholds (owners to submit proposed changes with data).

Quick reference checklist (starter)
- [ ] Agree pilots and owners
- [ ] Deploy telemetry SDK and validate metrics
- [ ] Create dashboards and alerts
- [ ] Run canary and validate error budget behavior
- [ ] Train on-call and support
- [ ] Document runbooks and Confluence pages

Open questions to resolve in kickoff
- Which product KPIs should be explicitly tied to SLO targets for each pilot? (conversion, latency-sensitive features)
- Is 28-day window appropriate for batch embedding jobs or do we need a custom window?
- Who owns provisioning increased tracing quota if needed (Billing/payments sign-off)?

Immediate next steps (this week)
- Schedule kickoff workshop and invite product leads for pilot candidates (Maya).
- Circulate SLO template draft (Arjun) and ask for feedback within 4 business days.
- Start telemetry SDK compatibility scan for pilot services (Lina).

Appendix: useful links and example queries
- Example Prometheus rule: recording rule for error_budget_burn: rate(errors[28d]) / rate(total_requests[28d])
- Honeycomb search example: trace.duration P99 over 28-day rolling window grouped by route
- Confluence template: Reliability SLO Team Template (linked_artifacts above)

Notes
- Keep this playbook light and iterative. The emphasis for the MVP is measurable improvement and a repeatable rollout pattern rather than perfect instrumentation across every service.
- When in doubt, prioritize visibility (dashboards + simple alerts) over complex automated remediation for the first two pilots.
